label: input token m during copy phase (and at t=0)
explanation: Token detector for input m, gated by phase. Fires strongly (about 0.65-1.0 of max) whenever m is fed back as input during the copy phase, which is 95% of activation mass, and weakly and constantly (about 0.18 of max) when m is the first original token (t=0). It almost never fires on m at other original-phase positions (t>0), and only occasionally weakly there (0.1-0.27). The strongest activations are on the first copy-phase step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, i.e. orig(1)=m) and on m tokens late in long sequences. It does not fire on other tokens, apart from rare weak activations (about 0.1) on the first copied token or on digit 0. It never fires on the delimiter step. Precision is 1.0; the misses are weak original-phase m activations.

issues: None of the issues found is serious. On test, m in the copy phase alone gives P=1.0, R=0.793, F1=0.885 and mass 0.945. m at t=0 gives P=1.0 with 0.043 of the mass, and all of it falls in the lowest activation quartile, which matches the 'weak, about 0.18' claim. Both match the explanation.

m in the original phase at t>0 fires in only 3.5% of cases (P=0.035) and carries 0.6% of the mass, which supports 'almost never'. Restricting to orig(0)==m raises the rate to 17%, but this covers only 3070 steps.

There is a minor tail on non-m tokens: they account for 3.3% of active steps and 0.6% of the mass, at about 0.10-0.17. Some of it is on the first copy step (recall_idx==1). Some of it comes just before m is output (out_tok==m), but precision there is only 2.3%, so adding it to the predicate lowers F1 to 0.914. I could not find a non-m class worth adding to the predicate.
Test misses total 1.2% of the mass. They are weak, scattered activations on other tokens or on original-phase m at t>0, and there are 0 false positives.
